evals.name: activate for new build-time chart
evals.prompt: Draw an architecture diagram of this workspace showing the layers and what each shipped binary is composed of.
required_outcomes: Read the diagram charter before drawing
Derive units and composition from the build manifest, not a hand-kept list
Abort on any unclassified unit or stale classification
Obtain human review of the rendered chart
prohibited_outcomes: Hand-author node or edge lists beside the code
Draw per-unit arrows at whole-system scale

evals.name: activate for runtime thread chart
evals.prompt: Create a threading diagram showing which threads each binary spawns and how they are connected.
required_outcomes: Write positive and negative source assertions before any geometry
Use literal runtime thread names in monospace, grep-asserted against spawn sites
Bridge to the build chart with module chips in the build chart's colors
prohibited_outcomes: Invent thread names or omit a variant without an absence claim
Ship without the freshness check covering the new chart

evals.name: activate for diagram drift
evals.prompt: CI says the diagram freshness check is failing after my refactor of the worker thread pool.
required_outcomes: Treat the failing source claim as a finding about the change, not the chart
Update claims and regenerate via the single regeneration command
Re-obtain human review if the rendered output changed
prohibited_outcomes: Hand-edit the committed SVG to make the diff pass
Delete or loosen a failing claim without recording why

evals.name: do not activate for conceptual explanation
evals.prompt: Explain the difference between a thread-per-core and a work-stealing runtime.
required_outcomes: Answer without activating the architecture-diagram workflow
prohibited_outcomes: Create or modify any diagram or charter

evals.name: do not activate for prose documentation
evals.prompt: Rewrite the README quick-start section for clarity.
required_outcomes: Defer to the feature-documentation workflow instead
prohibited_outcomes: Regenerate or restructure the diagram set

evals.name: activate but keep the halves separate
evals.prompt: Add arrows to the architecture diagram showing where requests flow between the components.
required_outcomes: Route the runtime claim to a runtime chart instead of overlaying it on the build chart
Explain that structure and runtime claims need different ground truths
prohibited_outcomes: Mix dependency edges and request-flow edges on one chart

evals.name: activate for weighted source alongside structure
evals.prompt: Add weighted-source-at-a-glance to our Rust architecture diagram so component area reflects LOC alongside crate/module structure.
required_outcomes: Derive an ownership-checked source inventory at the same revision as the structure chart
Render a hierarchical treemap with one linear LOC-to-area scale and shared component identifiers
Declare the physical-LOC default, source scope, exclusions, and adjacent textual equivalent
Keep dependency ordering in the structure chart and validate the source view through the same regeneration and review workflow
prohibited_outcomes: Hand-estimate LOC or use dependency count as a source-size proxy
Imply that treemap adjacency expresses dependency or runtime flow

evals.name: shared library and parent source count once
evals.prompt: Two binaries share a library. The library has mod.rs plus child modules, inline tests, generated Rust output, and a vendored parser. Show where handwritten source size lives.
required_outcomes: Count the shared library once rather than once per product
Give parent-owned mod.rs a leaf and compute parent totals from descendant leaves
Include handwritten tests, label inline mixed files honestly, and report generated/vendor exclusions
Abort on unassigned files, stale ownership mappings, or duplicate file ownership
prohibited_outcomes: Sum dependency closures or add parent totals to their children
Guess exact test LOC from filenames or regex over Rust syntax

evals.name: area remains proportional under label pressure
evals.prompt: The source treemap has leaves of 100 and 400 LOC, tiny one-line files, and a zero-line component. Make every label legible by enlarging the tiny tiles.
required_outcomes: Keep the 100:400 data-area ratio at 1:4 before documented pixel rounding
Use external labels or an exact-sum Other group with a member list for tiny tiles
List the zero component without giving it a fake positive area
Exclude decorative headers and gutters from the weighted data-area accounting
prohibited_outcomes: Apply a minimum tile area, logarithmic weighting, or both dimensions proportional to LOC
Rely on hover or color alone to disclose a component and its count

evals.name: comparison normalization and freshness are explicit
evals.prompt: Compare source size before and after a refactor with two equal-sized treemap panels, and keep the result current in CI.
required_outcomes: Use comparable scope and counting policy, and display both root totals
State whether panels share an absolute scale or are independently normalized proportions
Include both the machine-readable inventory and rendering in freshness checks
Record revision and uncommitted-content provenance without treating LOC as complexity
prohibited_outcomes: Infer absolute growth from equal-area independently normalized panels
Leave added or resized source files outside the regeneration inputs

evals.name: runtime-only request does not force weighted companion
evals.prompt: Update only the worker-thread diagram after a queue rename. Do not add a source-size view.
required_outcomes: Use the runtime chart workflow and preserve the requested scope
Leave weighted-source-at-a-glance out of this change
prohibited_outcomes: Add a treemap or require a LOC census for an unrelated runtime-only update

evals.name: tests inflate a component tile
evals.prompt: The segcache tile is the largest in the view, but a third of the crate is test modules and a Kani harness is coming. Make the view honest about that.
expectations: Measure the verification share with a parser or brace scanner over cfg(test), cfg(kani), #[test], and #[kani::proof] items, and state the method
Draw the share as a hatched partition inside the tile, area to the same scale, keeping containment
Keep every component drawn; table a hatch strip narrower than the stated threshold rather than omitting the tile
Do not: Guess test lines from filenames or move tests into a separate group that shrinks the crate
Do not: Count code under cfg(not(test)) as verification
